title: Formula sheet
html:
Every formula in the book, in plain text, with the chapter that explains it. m is the number of examples, n the number of features, alpha the learning rate, lambda the regularization strength.

Name Formula Chapter
Linear model, one feature f(x) = w x + b 4
Linear model, many features f(x) = w . x + b = w1 x1 + ... + wn xn + b 7
Squared-error cost J(w, b) = (1 / 2m) x sum of (f(x_i) - y_i)^2 5
RMSE square root of the mean of (f(x_i) - y_i)^2 5
R squared 1 - (error around the fit) / (error around the mean) 5
Gradient descent update w := w - alpha x dJ/dw, and b := b - alpha x dJ/db, both at once 6
Linear regression slopes dJ/dw_j = (1/m) x sum of (f(x_i) - y_i) x_ij; dJ/db = (1/m) x sum of (f(x_i) - y_i) 6, 7
Normal equation w = (X^T X)^-1 X^T y 7
Z-score (x - mean) / standard deviation 8, 15
Mean normalization (x - mean) / (max - min) 8
Polynomial model f(x) = w1 x + w2 x^2 + w3 x^3 + b 8
Sigmoid g(z) = 1 / (1 + e^-z) 9
Logistic regression model f(x) = g(w . x + b), the probability that y = 1 9
Odds and log-odds odds = p / (1 - p); ln(odds) = w . x + b 9
Log loss (one example) -log(f) if y = 1; -log(1 - f) if y = 0 10
Logistic cost J = -(1/m) x sum of [y log f + (1 - y) log(1 - f)] 10
Cost at w = 0, b = 0 ln 2 = 0.693 10
Regularized cost J + (lambda / 2m) x sum of w_j^2 11
Regularized update w_j := w_j - alpha [ (1/m) x sum of (f - y) x_j + (lambda/m) w_j ] 11
scikit-learn settings Ridge alpha = lambda; LogisticRegression C = 1 / lambda 11
Accuracy (TP + TN) / all 12
Precision TP / (TP + FP) 12
Recall TP / (TP + FN) 12
F1 2 x precision x recall / (precision + recall) 12
Neuron a = g(w . x + b) 14
Layer output, many rows A = g(X W + b); X is m by n, W is n by u, b has u numbers 14
Parameters in a dense layer u x (n + 1): n weights and one bias for each of u neurons 14
Gini impurity 1 - sum of p^2 over the classes; 0 is pure, 0.5 is a 50/50 split of two classes 13
Cosine similarity a . b / (length of a x length of b) 15, 18
Chain rule d/dw of (w x - y)^2 = 2 (w x - y) x 15
Bayes' theorem P(A given B) = P(B given A) x P(A) / P(B) 15
Reciprocal rank fusion score(chunk) = sum over lists of 1 / (k + rank), k = 60 18
hit@k the share of questions whose gold chunk is among the top k 18
